In a seedy motel room, Frederick's life was cruelly punctuated with a corkscrew, leaving Detective Winston to unravel the twisted tales of two suspects, Tessa and Van.

Winston's dispatch message included the name "Tessa". He remembered her as a skilled bartender at a high-end restaurant, famed for her unique way of handling a corkscrew, especially while opening extravagant wine bottles. Recently, she seemed to have been working outside of normal working hours. She was often seen requesting financial support from Frederick, an affluent regular customer who wouldn't mind doling out his means for attention.

A friend once mentioned to him Frederick’s intention to spill the beans about Tessa's grim reality. It was not every day someone aimed to settle a debt of that size, and the situation intrigued Winston. Using the information he had, he traced that Tessa had checked in the motel a couple of days before Frederick’s demise.

Winston pulled his sedan into the dusty lot of the low-rise motel on the outskirts of town. There he saw Tessa, emerging from a room and handing a key back to the motel manager. The motel staff confirmed that the implicating room was indeed paid for by Tessa, and their logbook showed that she had checked in before Frederick’s death. They also agreed that she had remained on the premises throughout.

The day Tessa was arrested, she displayed her usual calm demeanor. As the police handcuffed her, a metallic shine of a corkscrew slipped out from her apron pocket, landing on the ground below. This was her personal corkscrew, a tool she always had on hand for her routine work at the restaurant, and one that she was seen using frequently to open wine bottles during her shift.

As Winston left the motel to return to the precinct, he mused over the victim’s connection with Tessa. Frederick knew about Tessa’s considerable debt, and this was not ordinary behavior between a server and a regular patron. But for now, the facts just laid out the circumstances. His sole contribution to this puzzle would be to compile the facts so they could make sense. The rest — the swift execution of justice — was a matter of time. And Winston knew that time always brought the truth to light.

Winston straightened his tie as he approached the scene of Frederick's murder, squinting under the motel's harsh fluorescent lighting. Frederick, a successful events planner, was stealing lucrative contracts right from Van’s territory. On the other hand, Van also managed to poach a few of Frederick's prime clients. Frederick's competitors saw his success as the rising spark of a problem they had to deal with. Someone like Van, maybe. 

Van. The one who was always behind a desk at every event he planned, for some reason avoiding any kind of physical exertion. For instance, at every event, he could be found refusing a spot in the robust, physically-demanding relay races that colleagues customarily participated in. That night was no different, the event was a wine tasting. Van would likely be there, not participating in the traditional grape-stomping competition. There, Van would flaunt his newly-acquired clients; the ones he had usurped from Frederick.

With this thought in his head, Winston drove over to the event, arriving to the sight of Van pouring wine expediently with a corkscrew for the event attendees instead of joining in on the active games. 

"Van," Winston greeted, nodding at him.

"Detective," Van replied, raising an eyebrow. 

He paused as Winston took a seat in front of him, then offered a bottle of red. "Wine, Detective?"

"No, thanks," Winston said, "Don't you usually have an assistant to open wine bottles?"

Van laughed, shrugging off the observation easily. "I like doing it. It's therapeutic," he said.

Then there was the fresh dressing peeking out from under Van's cuff, the one he offered some vague explanation for, just like every other time Winston had seen him injured. He referred to these as ‘small accidents’.

He remembered what Van's colleagues had said about him. Always getting injured, never playing in any games, always behind a desk, and there was that thing with Frederick. 

"Frederick," Winston started, both men looking somber at the mention of the recent murder. Van averted his gaze, focusing steadfastly on the bottle he was opening.

"I heard you had a falling out."

Van sighed, and for the first time that evening he looked tired. "Fred and I... we had our differences. He was snatching clients right under my nose. And I wasn't just taking it lying down, I got back at him by snatching some of his clients,” he confessed. 

"Heard you even threatened him once," Winston said quietly.

"That was just business, nothing personal," Van replied coldly. "If you're suggesting--"

Winston lifted his hands, chuckling lightly. "I'm not suggesting anything, Van," he said carefully.

Turning his attention back to the bottle, Van popped the cork and poured himself a glass. "Fine. I had my disagreements with Frederick," he admitted. "Yes, we threatened each other over clients. But that's all it was... just threats."

Winston left shortly after, leaving Van to his wine and his thoughts. As he walked back to the car, he remembered the coroner's report. Those puncture wounds in Frederick's autopsy. Consistent with a corkscrew... 

A steady cold rain fell on Winston's windshield as he drove away, leaving behind the warm lights of the wine tasting event and a man with a lot on his mind.

In the unforgiving desert landscape, Philip's lifeless body was discovered, a nunchaku the ghastly cause of his demise, leaving Detective Winston on a barren hunt, with Jim and Woodrow as his prime suspects.

In the dimly lit office of Winston's chosen haven, the world spun as the crime scene photos of Philip were spread across the detective's desk. Alone in the desert, with the grim encore of death, Philip’s fate felt oddly disconnected from the realities of the bustling metropolis.

Winston pondered over the crucial facts concerning the deceased Philip, particularly those relating to a certain dockworker, Jim. He was reminded of the small piece of evidence that came along with a ledger found in Philip's frozen hands. The ledger chronicled complex illegal smuggling operations. Notably among those was crucial information that it detailed illegal smuggling operations that Jim was involved with at the docks, making the ledger belonging to Jim even more incriminating.

It was known that Jim often sought solitude in the quiet, sweeping desert that Philip was found. In fact, the day of Philip's death, it was known that Jim had spent a significant amount of time there in the desert, with Philip.

Winston resolved to head to the docks as his initial step. He knew Jim worked there, and was also an active participant in some form of martial arts training. The docks, apart from being a bustling hub of commerce, also had a lesser-known martial arts center. Additionally, Jim was known to be struggling under a heavy amount of debt, a large part of which he owed to Philip.

Upon arriving at the docks, Winston observed the various trading activities. He noticed all kinds of commodities, including weapons like nunchaku being moved around. He couldn't help but wonder if some of the strains from Jim's debt might be channelled into these unlawful acts, particularly the illicit smuggling operations that Jim was deeply entrenched with at the docks.

“Hey, Jim! your presence is needed!" announced Winston, drawing the attention of a towering, muscular figure.

“Wow, Winston, you seem all business today," replied Jim, affably, turning to face his visitor.

“You weren’t working today?” queried Winston, scrutinizing Jim's reaction. Giving a carefree shrug, Jim responded, "Yes, occasionally we get the day off, like today."

Jim's actions had a disciplined, well-practiced grace, something Winston noted was consistent with someone undergoing martial arts training. When Winston asked about his training, Jim confirmed it with a simple nod.

“So, what about the money you owed Philip?” Winston asked, causing a silence to fall over them, broken only by the sounds of crashing waves. The burden of the enormous debt to Philip weighed heavily on Jim, evidenced by his discomfort.

“Philip... He came across some... documents,” Jim confessed, his gaze focused elsewhere, “He planned to use them against me. Though, it's irrelevant now."

During their conversation, Winston learned Jim not only lazed around the desert, but on the day of Philip's death, he had spent a significant portion of the day there in the desert with Philip. Moreover, that happened to be a day when Jim had no work obligations elsewhere.

Soon, Winston found himself alone, watching as Jim left. After a moment’s contemplation, he figured his next action would be to visit the desert where Philip’s body was found.

Winston was walking towards the park with his hands in his pockets, dust from the trail whirling up around him as he went. His furrowed brows gave way to the seriousness he was to face discussing Philip's murder with his grandfather, Woodrow.

Woodrow was a frail looking old man. However, his frailty was physically deceptive. He was still as spry as a young deer when it came to his martial arts routine, he had been doing it every single day, religiously, after he had retired from forty long years of teaching martial arts. He was even sweating from his usual morning exercises when he walked up for their meeting.

"Winston, am I right?" Woodrow asked, nervously shifting his feet and clearing his throat constantly. To an observing party, it might almost look like nervous ticks. 

Winston nodded, not missing the unusual behavior, before he cleared his throat and asked, "You've lived in this small town all your life, Woodrow?" which the elderly man confirmed, stating that he had strong roots within his family and loved everyone fiercely. 

He held on to a coffee cup, which steamed slightly in the morning chill. He had been discussing the local park regulations with the passing-by officials while sipping slowly from the cup.

Interrupting their conversation was an unexpected arrival from a police officer, which resulted in Woodrow spilling his coffee on the cold concrete in surprise. 

After quick introductions and some reluctant banter, they walked towards Woodrow's weather-beaten house just outside the park. Inside, Winston couldn't help but get drawn towards the shelves, which displayed an array of martial arts-related memorabilia, many of which were used by Woodrow himself during his teaching years. His eyes fell on a pair of nunchaku kept securely within a glass case.

"Treasures from better times," Woodrow murmured looking at his collection.

The conversation soon shifted towards Philip. Philip, the man who had shown no remorse publicly humiliating Woodrow. Philip was a tough bone to crack, his abusive nature had managed to alienate not only Woodrow, but almost every member of their family.

"Philip was a tough man to deal with. But family is family, you know," said Woodrow before he excused himself to wash the coffee stain off his shirt. 

Winston was left staring at the array of martial arts memorabilia.

In the aftermath of a devastating home explosion that claims the life of Angela, seasoned Detective Winston hones in on two prime suspects: Patrick and Alvin.

Detective Winston winced a little as he pulled up to Angela's home. What was once a well kept, welcoming residence was now charred remains. All due to an explosion powerful enough to shake the neighborhood. As he began his investigation into the events leading up to the incident, one name kept surfacing: Patrick, local surfing instructor and part-time demolition worker who frequently had to handle, use, and was often training on disposing explosives at his job as a requirement of safety measures.
 
To understand this suspect more, Winston set off to meet the man at his next surfing lesson. Under the blistering sun, Patrick was there, quick to anger, bellowing at his students who seemed more frightened than focused on the waves. Several students have had grievances about his harsh teaching methods, which translated to Winston as a lack of patience.

When the session started, Winston noticed the scar that ran down the side of his face which looked ill-treated. Patrick noticed him too. His tall and sturdy figure smirked and sauntered towards Winston. "Detective, right?" his voice was rough, like sandpaper against a rough surface. "Heard about Angela, disturbing really." 

Patrick's nonchalance bothered Winston, but he gave an understanding nod. "Yeah, it is. You were doing demolition work part-time, handling and using explosives, and even have been frequently training on disposing of them, right? That could surely be a dangerous work, isn't it?" Winston queried.

"Sure is," Patrick answered, side-glancing towards his students who were still trying to catch a wave, "Just like surfing, you know, it's all about control." 

Later, Winston found out from the old records that Patrick once worked in a prison. An inmate had assaulted him, and despite being injured, he'd managed to subdue the prisoner. The incident had left him off fieldwork due to minor injuries, but his bravery had been noted. 

Winston also learned that Patrick borrowed a large sum of money from Angela. A neighbor heard Angela frequently threatening to call the cops on Patrick, but he was always around. Patrick had been seen near Angela's home that evening, the very scene of the explosion. There were no others found in the vicinity at the time.

Now, it seemed Winston was dealing with a surfing instructor who vented his frustrations on his students, an injured prison-personnel-turned-demolition-worker with frequent training on handling and disposing explosives who borrowed heavily from a woman who is now dead and was glimpsed around her house before the explosion. Interesting, certainly, but Winston knew there was more to uncover before any real pieces could begin to fall into place here. This was just the start.

Winston sat in his car, surveying through the battered fence that surrounded Angela's suburban home. The yellow tape marking off the scene of the crime fluttered eerily in the wind. Within that marked perimeter was devastation... an explosion had taken place there recently.

As Winston stepped out of his vehicle, a mail truck adorned with cheerful, vibrant colors pulled up to a house down the street. It was Alvin, a well-liked figure in the community, known best for his calm demeanor and reliability. Ex-military, he was now a delivery man and today, just like every day, he was doing his rounds. Along with the rumors of Alvin's unusual fascination with Angela and his tendency to lurk outside her home during unexpected hours, several witnesses had observed Alvin frequently retreating to his garage, where he kept a collection of various artifacts, including explosives and old photos of Angela.

Alvin had scheduled stops all over the neighborhood, but Angela - the victim in Winston's case - was one that he had on his list daily. It was on Alvin's delivery sheet that day too - a package was scheduled for Angela's house. Always punctual, Alvin would hand-deliver packages to Angela; she was always home to receive them, waiting for him at her front door with a box of his old photos of her flashed to Alvin’s mind. 

Angela's old housekeeper clued Winston in on something else. She sat, frail and teary-eyed, as she told him that Angela had recently filed a restraining order against Alvin. Despite this, he continued to visit her home with deliveries daily, revealing a persistence that bordered on stalking. 

"I learned about a lot of things in the army, Winston. How to survive on tinned beans, how to make a fire, how to assemble a rifle... Yes, I might have learnt a bit about explosives too, and have some at my place, but they're never intended for any harm," Alvin responds, visibly tense.

Winston catches sight of the mail truck and the single, small box addressed to Angela seated in the front. It was clear the last delivery of the day was made to her and it was also known that Angela was there to receive it. Angela's neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, a nosy old lady who saw everything on the block had testified to Angela personally receiving the parcel at around the same time the explosion incident occurred.

Long after Winston had left, Alvin continued to stare at the spot where Winston had been sitting, his calm exterior shattered. With dread, he remembered the package marked "explosive" in his garage, along with a stack of Angela's old photos, and the parcel he had delivered just days before Angela's house had gone up in flames.

In the tranquil sphere of the temple, Charlotte's demise by barbed wire disrupts the serenity, drawing Detective Winston into a puzzling web woven by suspects Priscilla and Xenia.


Winston unfolded the clipped newspaper announcement of Charlotte's upcoming wedding. He scanned the quaint details, turning each over in his mind. The setting was a temple, a peculiar choice within their community. Unique also, was the choice of Xenia as the wedding planner. A woman known for her fastidiousness and deft hands in crafting seamless events. 

In a recent chat with Charlotte before her wedding, she mentioned a peculiar detail regarding a certain secret she was advised by Xenia to keep hidden - her past relationship with Xenia's current partner. It was a secret she was planning to unveil at the altar, a revelation that would surely raise a few eyebrows, with Xenia no longer being the lone keeper of it.

"Ms. Xenia, I presume?" Winston asked, entering the wedding planner's office. 

"Yes. How can I aid you detective?" Xenia responded, with a slight surprise in her eyes.

"I wanted to talk about Charlotte's wedding... a ceremony that was slated to occur at the exact minute of her murder. Noticed anything unusual around those days?” Winston queried.

Xenia hesitated, her expression wavering. It was clear that the jab about Charlotte's intention to confess the past, which involved Xenia's significant other, had struck a nerve. The anger simmering in Xenia's eyes was volatile and intense, enough to make anyone uncomfortable.

As they conversed, Winston's attention drifted to an office closet, slightly ajar. A suitcase peeked from within, stuffed with neatly folded clothes, almost as though it was constantly ready for a trip. His colleagues had often mentioned seeing this suitcase during their routine meetings with Xenia.

"Ever much of a traveler, Xenia?" Winston asked casually. 

She seemed taken aback by his question. "Sometimes... it's part of the job. Last minute trips for a desired decoration, or perhaps to get a gift. Weekend trips and all."

"That your suitcase in the closet, always packed and ready?" Winston nodded towards it. Xenia followed his gaze toward the suitcase, then back at him. "Yes, why?" 

"No reason," Winston shrugged. "It’s just that colleagues have mentioned spotting you with your luggage at the airport, and at the train station buying tickets – during work hours."

"Yeah, like I said, travelling becomes part of the job sometimes,” countered Xenia, smoothly.

Throughout their conversation about wedding preparations, Xenia specified that she was responsible for every minute detail – setting up and breaking down the décor, liaising with the temple people, overseeing every aspect of the event. She emphasized that her duties required her presence before, during, and after the ceremony. Winston mentally jotted this down, noticing how neatly these timings coincided with those of Charlotte's unfortunate fate.

Winston rose to depart, conveying his gratitude, "Thanks for your time."

"Of course, anything to help," Xenia replied softly. “Charlotte's passing is shocking, but remember, we rely on trust and reputation in our business. It's all we have. Charlotte's confession could have marred that."

Detective Winston sifted through the papers littering his desk. Crime scene photos mixed with witness statements and information on both the victim, Charlotte, and the potential suspect, Priscilla. Winston ran a hand through his hair, taking a deep breath.

Eyewitness accounts placed Priscilla at the temple on the day of the crime. The same temple where Charlotte was found, her life taken by barbed wire. Winston's gaze drifted towards some photos of the hiking trails Priscilla was known to frequent. The trails, all too often, wound their way past the same temple where Charlotte met her end.

Pushing the papers around, Winston found a report from the local police. Priscilla's involvement with certain gang activities was far from a well-kept secret. The faded gang tattoos on Priscilla's skin were testament to her affiliation. Charlotte, on the other hand, was part of a rival gang, a fact anyone could see from the tags she left behind. 

Photos from the trails Priscilla often hiked showed a significant amount of barbed wire fencing. Winston mused, barbed wire was indeed common along these trails - so much so that Priscilla had even learned to utilize items like it in her own survival knowledge on these hiking expeditions. 

A picture of Priscilla hiking caught Winston's attention. He noted the pair of wire snips she carried. Those would be potentially useful in dealing with the surplus of barbed wire on her usual trails. He also noted the rough timeline on the police report. Charlotte's time of death matched up too neatly with the time witnesses had spotted Priscilla at the temple that day.

"Interesting, isn't it?" Winston muttered to himself, mulling over the facts at hand. Pushing his chair back, he decided it was time to ask Priscilla some questions. He was determined to learn the truth, one piece of evidence at a time.

In the once tranquil mosque, tragedy struck as Jamal was brutally shot dead, and now it's up to Detective Winston to weave through the tangled web of secrets Mark and Gerald are entwined in.

Winston lingered at the fringes of the mosque's gates, studying the CCTV footage on his portable monitor. He was trying to absorb the details, trying to get a feel of the timeline. The footage showed Mark, a well-known local lawyer, clearly entering the mosque before the murder.

Mark was a regular attendee at the mosque for Friday prayers, and the timestamped security footage reinforced that this day was no different.

With a deep sigh, Winston packed up the monitor and made his way to the local store, where he'd arranged to meet with the store's clerks. He'd heard from the community that the quiet lawyer had been seen buying ammunition there.

The clerks confirmed it. Yes, Mark had been to the store to buy shotgun shells. It wasn’t out of place for Mark, known for his involvement with a myriad of firearm-related cases.

As Winston traveled back to his office, he reflected on the conversation he had earlier with Mark. The attorney was an influential figure in the community and often worked on cases involving firearm charges. His knowledge amassed from representing law enforcement personnel showed in his knowledgeable chatter about firearms. 

In their conversation, Mark's fear was evident. It stemmed from Jamal, the victim, who openly expressed extremist beliefs to the community, causing unease. Mark was tasked with ensuring the safety of many community members, and they’d expressed their worries about Jamal to him clearly.

Upon reaching his office, Winston began to piece together the case. He recalled at the time of the incident, Mark was present at the mosque, taking part in prayers along with the others. And Jamal… was Jamal afraid? Thought Winston. The following days would need more thorough investigation. With the data on his desk, the detective prepared himself to slowly trace his way through truth and deception in the days to come.

Winston found himself parked outside the confines of a building overflowing with culture and history - a Mosque, that now is stained with the gruesome murder of Jamal. The wind threatened to dishevel his hair as he made his way inside, crossing paths with Gerald, a violinist who frequented the same religious establishment.

"Gerald, right?" Winston called over the gusty winds, obtaining the attention of the musician.

"Yes, that's me." Gerald nodded, inspecting his violin case as though he could see through it to its contoured resident within.

"You were seen entering the Mosque at an interesting time by the security tapes, Gerald." Winston stated, keeping his gaze steady upon the man.

"Interesting time, detective?" Gerald raised a questioning brow, "I regularly come here for my prayers around this time."

Nodding, Winston eyed the violin case again, "This—a hobby for you or profession?"

"Profession. It consumes a lot of my time but I wouldn't trade it away for anything else,” Gerald responded, traces of pride crossing his features, as his fingers brushed lightly across the case. "Keeps your fingers nimble, doesn't it?" Winston asked casually.

"Absolutely," Gerald responded, smiling softly, "I suppose you could say they're suited to other delicate tasks too."

Winston's gaze darted back to Gerald's face. "Delicate tasks like...?"

"Oh, anything that requires intricate finger movements I suppose.”

This was the first time in a long time anyone had invoked curiosity in Winston, a pleasant change amidst the tragedy. Before he could indulge in this observation, a glint from a computer screen in the corner caught his eye.

“Is that public?” Winston inclined his head towards the computer.

"Why yes, Detective, it's open to all - centerpiece of this quaint little library corner," Gerald explained, before whispering in a reverential tone, "It's perfect for uninterrupted reading."

"Reading anything interesting?"

"Well, I have been immersing myself in the lives of some outstanding violinists who passed away recently. I find a kind of fascination in death, you know."

"Interesting," Winston simply responded, not daring to let a single emotion cross his face. 

Casually resting his hand on Gerald’s shoulder, Winston asked, “Gerald, do you by chance ever go to the shooting range?” 

“Funny you should ask," he answered casually, "I just bought a shotgun last week.”

“Well then," Winston said in a light tone, "maybe I’ll see you around there.”

With that, he let Gerald get back to his life. Taking one last look around the Mosque, Winston exited the building, his mind already buzzing with the next steps of his investigation.

In the sleepy town of Mapleton, the unusual murder of Stella by a nunchaku in her own kitchen has set the stage for Detective Winston's most perplexing case yet.

An early morning home visit to investigate a disturbing crime scene had now transitioned into a late afternoon at a strikingly unique boutique-like office.

The buzz of industrial sewing machines filled the detective's ear as he entered. The high ceilings, hung with bolts of fabric in every imaginable hue, touched upon the unique operation run within these walls. Winston squinted against the gleaming steel fixtures and sharp angles of modern decor. Models stood like long-legged statues, being prodded, pinned, and fussed over by diligent seamstresses, while students on internship from nearby colleges, huddled together over laptops and design sketches near an overflowing rubbish bin. 

Suddenly, Winston caught sight of live security footage from a group of local colleges. All of them were pointed at Emma's studio, and all seemed to be focused on the same event, Emma abruptly closing her computer. Curious, he viewing the footage retrospectively, and, indeed, she had closed her computer abruptly several times in the past days.

She appeared from a curtained alcove at the back of the space, shutting her laptop abruptly once more as she noticed the detective’s arrival. Emma, fashion designer extraordinaire. 

"Why the visit, Winston?" Her nonchalant tone betrayed a perplexing mix of audacity and unease. 

"Just following up on some loose ends," he replied, his gaze trained on the computer she just closed and the designs she was now carrying in her arms. He asked to see them. 

Emma shuffled nervously and hurriedly tucked them back in her bag.

"I hear you've been working late nights recently," He said, attempting to keep the conversation flowing casually. "Your neighbors mentioned seeing your studio lights on until the early hours."

"Yeah, you know us designers. Night is when the inspiration hits."

Her assistant, a young woman with dyed hair, glanced up and gave her a guarded look before quickly shutting her laptop. Winston noticed, but moved on.

"I understand you were at Stella's house today. For a fitting in her kitchen, I believe?"

Emma nodded, her eyes flicking to the two college interns hunched over a laptop nearby who abruptly closed their devices and busied themselves with the tasks before them.

"She liked her fittings at home. Something about the comfort of her own kitchen," Emma said with a distant gaze.

"Yes. Odd place to hold a fitting, a kitchen. Odd place to find her too." The silence hung in the air like lead. "Have you been accused of plagiarism recently?"

The question felt sudden, but Emma's reaction was more telling. 

"Well...yes, Stella thought I was copying her designs. Stella found my sketches of her upcoming collection when she was at my studio last. She thought I had stolen them, but it was a misunderstanding. She threatened to expose me, but I didn't--"

"Odd," Winston interrupted. "She told me she found something hidden in your studio. Pages from a sketchbook, designs that looked remarkably like her unreleased collection." 

Emma was quiet. Winston continued, "Stella was alone in her kitchen most mornings. And that's where she found herself this morning."

Emma said nothing. 

The hum of sewing machines filled the room. Winston turned to walk away but paused, "One final thing, Emma, your business relies heavily on the internet, right?"

"Yes. It's common these days."

"Mmm. Might want to be careful what you leave open on your computers around here. I saw the way your assistant and the college interns noticed when you abruptly closed your browser." 

With that, Winston spun on his heel, and strode out of the bustling workspace leaving one very worried fashion designer behind.

Winston took a deep breath before ringing the bell on the townhouse's front door. Milton graciously accepted the detective into his home and offered him a seat in the sitting room. Gathering his thoughts, Winston began his informal interview.

"Milton, it is my understanding that you were at Stella's for dinner on the night of the murder, which took place in her kitchen. Is that correct?"

Milton nodded, “Yes, that's correct. I used to visit her quite often for dinner. She was a dear friend of mine,”.

Winston could detect slight distress in his voice and a gentleness in his eyes. He decided to switch topics. 

"I hear you’re quite the chemist?"

Milton, relieved by the change of conversation, brightened. "Yes, I've been practicing chemistry for a few decades now. I really enjoy it, makes understanding the world around us a bit easier."

Winston's attention shifted momentarily to a picture frame on a nearby bookshelf; Milton in a martial arts uniform, multiple medals hanging around his neck. He picked it up and inquired. 

"I see you're into martial arts too. Do you train often?" 

Milton smiled at the fond memory, "Ah, yes. I train regularly. For about fifteen years now. Got me a certification too. Helps keep the mind and body balanced you know.”

Winston, not noticing Milton's boast about his certification, continued to explore the room with his eyes. On a small table by the window, he spotted a pair of nunchaku. 

"Martial arts, eh?" Winston held up the nunchaku, Milton watched with a knowing smile.

"Yes, nunchaku is an essential part of martial arts, I practice with those regularly.”

A moment of silence endured with only the weather outside providing a subtle humming to the room. Winston decided it was time to tap the unspoken tension.

"And Milton…," Winston leaned forward, "You were aware that Stella had discovered concrete evidence and was planning to expose your fraudulent practices in your work, weren’t you?"

Milton swallowed audibly before answering. "Yes, Stella had found concrete evidence of my unethical practices at work which she didn’t agree with, and was planning to expose me. My dear friend was indeed honorable like that…”

Winston leaned back, processing this information silently. 

And without a word, Winston excused himself from the room.

In the tranquil vineyards, Terry's life was brutally snuffed out by a makeshift shiv, and now it's up to seasoned Detective Winston to unravel the truth from suspects Bella and Jose.

The vineyard was unusually crowded as Winston steadily emerged from his car. Workers swarmed around an old bulldozer — an earsplitting roar clearly disrupting their conversation.

Leading towards the shade of the makeshift structure, Jose — a construction worker at the scene, caught Winston's eye. His brow was furrowed in worry. Laments about his diminishing performance at work were ripe among his co-workers. Noticing a murder of crows flocking in the field, an eerie feeling washed over Winston.

Approaching the blue-collar worker, Winston kicked-off casually, "Got a minute, Jose?"

Drawing a deep breath, Jose turned around to shrug, he seemed a bit frazzled. His friendly banter with his co-workers cut short due to a bulldozer malfunctioning, "It's an early lunch... not like I was doing much today. My boss caught me chattin' instead of workin'."

Chuckling, Jose bobbed towards the group of his co-workers, who were noticeably enjoying their conversation. "We've been going at it round the clock to get that wine store ready. Work's been tough lately, my performance has taken a hit, we gotta vent, right?"

"Yes, of course," Winston agreed, casually adding, "Isn't Terry your boss?"

"Technically, yes," sighed Jose, rubbing his neck nervously. "He owns this whole place," gesturing around the vineyard. "We had a... disagreement this morning. He accused me of stealing from the building site, falsifying work hours. Even threatened to fire me."

As Jose's voice trailed off, Winston observed, "Sounds tough."

"Yes, sir," Jose replied quietly. "The man even suspects me for the murder that happened here last week, during my shift. If Terry fires me... everything comes crashing down. This is the main work I've got right now... I can't afford to lose it."

Winston nodded understandingly and asked him if Terry, who was also present during the murder event, was around the vineyard at this time, to which Jose confirmed.

After reassuring Jose, he'd look into the matter, Winston began walking towards his car. Just as he was leaving, the obnoxious screech of the faulty bulldozer marked the end of an early lunch break.

Winston sipped his black coffee as he stared out of his aging police cruiser, eyeing the sprawling vineyard and thinking about Terry. Reports had come in of a heated exchange between Terry and Bella. A scenario that happened right after Terry caught Bella red-handed with a bottle of rare, expensive wine she hadn't paid for. An intern.
